dimensions.assessment: Affects VA employees responsible for acquiring, managing, or implementing software assets, alongside IT leadership.
dimensions.evidence: The Secretary shall ensure that each employee responsible for acquiring, managing, or implementing software assets receives training no less often than annually

dimensions.assessment: Aims to eliminate waste, fraud, and abuse in software licensing and procurement, track inventories, and achieve cost savings.
dimensions.evidence: Identifying and eliminating waste, fraud, and abuse, including by regularly comparing the inventory... to identify discrepancies, over-procurement, redundant purchases

dimensions.assessment: Explicitly prohibits additional appropriations, requiring implementation with existing funds while aiming to generate cost savings.
dimensions.evidence: This section shall be implemented using existing personnel, systems, and funds. This section does not authorize additional appropriations

dimensions.assessment: Amends title 38, United States Code, to mandate a department-wide software asset management policy, reviews, training, annual reporting, and a 5-year sunset.
dimensions.evidence: Subchapter II of chapter 5 of title 38, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new section

dimensions.assessment: Establishes policy requirements and annual reports that sunset five years after the date of enactment.
dimensions.evidence: The requirements and authorities of this section shall terminate on the date that is five years after the date of the enactment of the VAMOSA Act.

importance_detail.rationale: The bill requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to establish a comprehensive department-wide software asset management policy, maintain software inventories, provide annual training, and report cost savings, utilizing existing resources and personnel.
